title: 2 Chronicles 2: Solomon Prepares to Build the House
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Chronicles 2](/bible/2-chronicles/2)

**[2 Chronicles 2:1-2](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v1)</sup> And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v2)</sup> And Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them.

- Solomon determined to build a house for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom. Where did Solomon get this understanding and this vision. It came from his father David, who charged him to build the house.
- Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them. This is the same labor force spoken of again at the end of the chapter.
- David had told Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, warning that if he sought Him he would be found, but if he forsook Him he would be cast off. David then gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Chronicles 28:9](/bible/1-chronicles/28#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/1-chronicles/28#v9)</sup> And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the Lord searcheth all hearts, and understandeth all the imaginations of the thoughts: if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever.

    David charged Solomon to know the God of his father and serve him with a perfect heart, for the Lord searcheth all hearts.
  - **[1 Chronicles 28:11](/bible/1-chronicles/28#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/1-chronicles/28#v11)</sup> Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof, and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat,

    David gave Solomon the pattern of the porch, the houses, the treasuries, the chambers, and the place of the mercy seat.

**[2 Chronicles 2:3-10](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v3)</sup> And Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, As thou didst deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him an house to dwell therein, even so deal with me.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v4)</sup> Behold, I build an house to the name of the Lord my God, to dedicate it to him, and to burn before him sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of the Lord our God. This is an ordinance for ever to Israel.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v5)</sup> And the house which I build is great: for great is our God above all gods.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v6)</sup> But who is able to build him an house, seeing the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain him? who am I then, that I should build him an house, save only to burn sacrifice before him?
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v7)</sup> Send me now therefore a man cunning to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass, and in iron, and in purple, and crimson, and blue, and that can skill to grave with the cunning men that are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father did provide.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v8)</sup> Send me also cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees, out of Lebanon: for I know that thy servants can skill to cut timber in Lebanon; and, behold, my servants shall be with thy servants,
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v9)</sup> Even to prepare me timber in abundance: for the house which I am about to build shall be wonderful great.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v10)</sup> And, behold, I will give to thy servants, the hewers that cut timber, twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.

- Solomon sent to Huram king of Tyre, asking him to deal with him as he had dealt with David his father, sending cedars to build a house. Solomon purposed to build a house to the name of the Lord to dedicate to Him, to burn sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread and burnt offerings.
- The offerings Solomon named, morning and evening, on the sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, are ordained forever to Israel. This is why we keep them in the land of our captivity, rehearsing the righteous acts of the Most High according to the law given through Moses in the book of Numbers.
- The daily offering was two lambs, one in the morning and one in the evening; the sabbath offering added two more lambs; the new moon at the beginning of the months had its own burnt offering; and the solemn feasts followed, including the passover at even on the fourteenth day of the first month and the feast of unleavened bread beginning the fifteenth day.
- Solomon confessed that the house he built was great, for great is our God above all gods, yet the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain Him. He asked Huram for a cunning man to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, and colored cloth, and for cedar, fir, and algum trees out of Lebanon, promising wheat, barley, wine, and oil to the hewers.

  Precepts:
  - **[Numbers 28:3](/bible/numbers/28#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/numbers/28#v3)</sup> And thou shalt say unto them, This is the offering made by fire which ye shall offer unto the Lord; two lambs of the first year without spot day by day, for a continual burnt offering.

    Two lambs of the first year without spot were offered day by day for a continual burnt offering.
  - **[Numbers 28:9](/bible/numbers/28#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/numbers/28#v9)</sup> And on the sabbath day two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof:

    On the sabbath day two lambs of the first year were offered, beside the continual burnt offering.
  - **[Numbers 28:11](/bible/numbers/28#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/numbers/28#v11)</sup> And in the beginnings of your months ye shall offer a burnt offering unto the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, seven lambs of the first year without spot;

    In the beginning of their months Israel offered a burnt offering unto the Lord, which is the new moon.
  - **[Numbers 28:16](/bible/numbers/28#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/numbers/28#v16)</sup> And in the fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord.

    In the fourteenth day of the first month is the passover of the Lord.
  - **[Leviticus 23:5](/bible/leviticus/23#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/23#v5)</sup> In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.

    In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, the day being reckoned from even to even.
  - **[Judges 5:11](/bible/judges/5#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/judges/5#v11)</sup> They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, even the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel: then shall the people of the Lord go down to the gates.

    In the places of drawing water they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, as we do in captivity.

**[2 Chronicles 2:11-16](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v11)</sup> Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because the Lord hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v12)</sup> Huram said moreover, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for the Lord, and an house for his kingdom.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v13)</sup> And now I have sent a cunning man, endued with understanding, of Huram my father’s,
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v14)</sup> The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving, and to find out every device which shall be put to him, with thy cunning men, and with the cunning men of my lord David thy father.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v15)</sup> Now therefore the wheat, and the barley, the oil, and the wine, which my lord hath spoken of, let him send unto his servants:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v16)</sup> And we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as thou shalt need: and we will bring it to thee in floats by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it up to Jerusalem.

- Huram the king of Tyre answered Solomon in writing, blessing the Lord God of Israel that made heaven and earth, who had given David a wise son endued with prudence and understanding to build a house for the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
- Huram sent a cunning man named Huram, skilful to work in gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, timber, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and to grave any manner of graving. Here it says he was the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan.
- The same history in First Kings 7 says this workman was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali. There is no contradiction: his mother was of the tribe of Naphtali, but she was of the city of Dan, which lay within the land of Naphtali. This is cleared up by using the Bible dictionary and the maps, and by chasing the references.
- The children of Dan had gone up and taken the city of Laish, also called Leshem, smiting it with the edge of the sword and renaming it Dan after their father. Israel had put the nations to tribute rather than driving them out as the Lord commanded, but the city itself sat in the borders of Naphtali, so a woman there could be spoken of both ways.
- Huram promised to cut wood out of Lebanon as much as Solomon needed and bring it in floats by sea to Joppa, from where it would be carried up to Jerusalem. These floats are like the large cargo ships and barges seen today upon the rivers and the seas.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Kings 7:14](/bible/1-kings/7#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/7#v14)</sup> He was a widow’s son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass: and he was filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and wrought all his work.

    The workman was a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, his father a man of Tyre, filled with wisdom to work in brass.
  - **[Judges 18:29](/bible/judges/18#v29)**
    > <sup>[29](/bible/judges/18#v29)</sup> And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the first.

    The children of Dan called the name of the city Dan after their father, though the name of the city was Laish at the first.
  - **[Joshua 19:47](/bible/joshua/19#v47)**
    > <sup>[47](/bible/joshua/19#v47)</sup> And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.

    The children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, took it, and called it Dan after the name of their father.

**[2 Chronicles 2:17-18](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v17)</sup> And Solomon numbered all the strangers that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them; and they were found an hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-chronicles/2#v18)</sup> And he set threescore and ten thousand of them to be bearers of burdens, and fourscore thousand to be hewers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people a work.

- Solomon numbered all the strangers in the land of Israel, after the numbering David his father had made, and they were found a hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred.
- He set threescore and ten thousand of them to bear burdens, fourscore thousand to be hewers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people a work. This is the same labor force named at the beginning of the chapter.
- David had prepared for the house long before, telling Solomon that in his trouble he had laid up a hundred thousand talents of gold, a thousand thousand talents of silver, brass and iron without weight, timber and stone, and workmen in abundance. Solomon did not begin empty-handed; his father had provided the workers and the materials.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Chronicles 22:9](/bible/1-chronicles/22#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/1-chronicles/22#v9)</sup> Behold, a son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.

    The Lord promised David a son, Solomon, who would be a man of rest, having peace and quietness given to Israel in his days.
  - **[1 Chronicles 22:14](/bible/1-chronicles/22#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/1-chronicles/22#v14)</sup> Now, behold, in my trouble I have prepared for the house of the Lord an hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver; and of brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance: timber also and stone have I prepared; and thou mayest add thereto.

    In his trouble David prepared for the house of the Lord gold, silver, brass, iron, timber, and stone in abundance.
  - **[Micah 4:10](/bible/micah/4#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/micah/4#v10)</sup> Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon; there shalt thou be delivered; there the Lord shall redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.

    Israel is told to go forth out of the city, for this is not our rest while our enemies still afflict us.
